claim.claim-text: a catheter tube having a tip end and a distal end; and a wetting mechanism operably coupled at or proximal to the tip end of the catheter tube for wetting the catheter tube, in use, the wetting mechanism comprising:

a housing forming a gripping element for the catheter, the housing being configured to be positioned initially at or proximal to the tip end of the catheter tube; wherein the housing comprises a wetting chamber into which at least a portion of the catheter tube is able to be introduced and be moved therethrough to move at least a portion of the catheter tube through the wetting chamber, in use; and wherein the wetting mechanism comprises a wetting applicator positioned within the wetting chamber configured to hold fluid therein and release said fluid to wet the catheter tube upon movement of the tube through the wetting chamber, wherein the wetting applicator comprises a baffle arrangement, and wherein the catheter tube comprises, is integrated with, or is coated with a hydrophilic component.
2. The catheter of claim 1 wherein the hydrophilic component is configured to provide a low friction outer surface of the catheter tube upon application of the wetting fluid.
3. The catheter of claim 1 or claim 2 wherein the hydrophilic component comprises a hydrophilic polymer.
4. The catheter of any preceding claim wherein the catheter is an intermittent urinary catheter.

5. The catheter of any preceding claim wherein the baffle arrangement defines a plurality of subregions of the wetting applicator each configured to hold a portion of the fluid held within the wetting applicator.
6. The catheter of claim 5 wherein the baffle arrangement defines a plurality of subregions within the wetting chamber in which the fluid may reside and/or be released into.
7. The catheter of any preceding claim wherein the wetting applicator comprises a flexible, compressible and/or resilient material.

8. The catheter of claim 7 wherein the wetting applicator is deformable under the application of a force thereto; and wherein deformation of the wetting applicator causes release of fluid held therein.

9. The catheter of any preceding claim, wherein the housing comprises a holding chamber containing a volume of wetting fluid therein, and wherein the wetting chamber is fluidly connected or connectable to the holding chamber, and wherein the wetting mechanism comprises a fluid release control component operable, in use, to control release of the fluid from the holding chamber into the wetting chamber.

10. The catheter of claim 9 wherein the fluid release control component comprises a container positioned within or at least partially defining the holding chamber and having the fluid contained therein, and wherein the container is rupturable or otherwise openable to release fluid contained therein.

11. The catheter of claim 10, wherein the wetting mechanism is configured such that the container may be ruptured or otherwise opened, in use, upon a user compressing, bending and/or flexing the housing.

12. The catheter of any of claims 9 to 11 wherein the fluid release control component comprises a moveable plug, moveable between a first position wherein it prevents release of the fluid from the holding chamber to the wetting chamber and/or the wetting applicator, and a second position wherein it allows release of the fluid from the holding chamber to the wetting chamber and/or the wetting applicator.

13. The catheter of any preceding claim further comprising a funnel provided at or proximal to the distal end of the catheter tube, with the wetting mechanism and funnel being separate components coupled via the catheter tube.

14. The catheter of claim 13 wherein the catheter comprises a sleeve formed of a film of plastics material positioned about the catheter tube, defining an internal volume about at least a portion of the catheter tube; the sleeve being coupled at a first end to the wetting mechanism and at a second, opposing end to the funnel.
15. A sealed packaged catheter according to any preceding claim, wherein the wetting mechanism is operably coupled at or proximal to the tip end of the catheter tube within the sealed package.
